ThingDef.label: hell's lantern
ThingDef.description: A great, slow, segmented worm-thing the size of a muffalo, its back studded with swollen pods that glow a sickly orange in the dusk of the root-maze. The hell's lantern crawls through the Miasma at barely a walking pace, grazing, paying no attention to anything around it — and it does not need to. Its mandibles carry a venom that leaves anything bitten sick and weakened, and every creature in the delta has learned to leave it be. The glowing pods can be milked for a luminous goo.

ThingDef.label: aaroxis dendoria
ThingDef.description: Uniquely engineered for life in an underground environment, this moth has been altered to produce silk even in adulthood, at the cost of remaining wingless.

ThingDef.label: bloodletter petrel
ThingDef.description: Uniquely adapted amongst the other wild creatures in polluted environments. Rather than feeding off potentially toxic flesh or plant matter, it instead prefers to feed off the blood of its prey.

ThingDef.label: luttaq
ThingDef.description: A long, soft-bodied crawler that is a caterpillar in every way but one: it never pupates. It simply goes on growing, breeding as a larva, until it is as long as a man is tall. It walks on rank after rank of stubby suckered prolegs, and its head is ringed by a crown of pale, groping tentacles that taste the ground ahead and draw plant matter in to the mouth. The body is the dull ochre and clay-brown of the flats it grazes, which makes the markings all the worse: along each segment runs a pattern of dark rings and staring false eyes that seem, from a distance, to shift and blink as the animal ripples forward.

ThingDef.label: foundry beetle
ThingDef.description: While herbivorous, this beetle is no easy prey. It uses its massive mandibles to crush both rival mates and anything that tries to hunt it. These beetles are often bred as war bugs by the more vicious cave dwellers.

ThingDef.label: gristle
ThingDef.description: A long, flat-plated burrower the length of a man, every segment carrying a pair of short digging legs and the head armoured in a heavy, shovel-edged shield. A gristle travels under the soil faster than most things can run above it, and hunts by feel: it rises under whatever it hears walking, seizes it in hooked mandibles and drags it down. Its body is mostly tough, rubbery muscle over a chitin frame, which is how it got its name. Unlike most many-legged things it bears its young alive.

ThingDef.label: moss beetle
ThingDef.description: A large, moss-flecked beetle that grazes low vegetation in damp, sheltered patches of scrub. Its meat is edible, if unremarkable.

ThingDef.label: fang leaf
ThingDef.description: Massive compared to its progenitor, the venus flytrap, the fang leaf is named for the way it snags prey the size of humans between jaws grown from a single leaf. It has managed to develop proto-feet and can move very slowly to more food-rich environments. This all tends to terrify people.

ThingDef.label: screecher
ThingDef.description: Mutated by pollution, this corvid has gained the ability to stun its prey using its cries while it attacks. It tends to hunt in packs.

ThingDef.label: bunker bug
ThingDef.description: Whether it is engineered or mutated from a wild animal is unknown, but this massive insect-like creature can use its powerful claws to rend its way through steel almost as easily as flesh and bone. It does not breed in captivity.

ThingDef.label: kroffa
ThingDef.description: A hardy, squat six-legged herbivore built for wasteland grazing. Its broad, low-slung barrel body rides on three pairs of short thick legs, hide overlapping in tough plates rather than fur, and its blunt insectile face works small mandible-like mouthparts around a pair of thick backward-curling horns. Docile enough to farm, and its milk is prized despite - or because of - how little the animal itself resembles anything back home.

ThingDef.label: megaphorid maggot
ThingDef.description: The larval form of the megaphorid fly. It is extremely ravenous and not very dangerous on its own, but they are rarely if ever found as such. They are most often found having burst out of an infected animal.

ThingDef.label: qattora
ThingDef.description:
A heavy, slow ground beetle of the cracked flats, built like a cask. Through the wet weeks a qattora gorges on bloom nectar, sap and anything sweet it can lap from the flood carpet, then stores the surplus in a swollen, rubbery abdomen that can reach the size of a fist. When the land dries it digs into the clay and lives off that reserve for months. Farmers keep them for the amber, faintly sweet fluid that can be coaxed from a full replete.
A qattora does not fight well, but it does not need to: struck or seized, it fires a scalding, choking spray from glands at the tip of its abdomen, a dense irritant cloud that leaves attackers blind and coughing while it lumbers away.

ThingDef.label: qetta
ThingDef.description: Something like a rodent, if a rodent had been assembled from the wrong parts. A qetta has no forelimbs at all: it bounds on two long, many-jointed hind legs, its body sheathed in overlapping plates of glossy chitin that slide over one another as it bends, coils and doubles back on itself in ways no backbone should allow. Its long, naked tail is fully prehensile and does the work hands would — hooking stems, hauling seed heads down to its mouth, anchoring it upside down in a crack while it feeds. It moves in bursts too quick to follow and freezes between them, and a flood-week flat can be thick with them without a single one ever quite being seen.

ThingDef.label: sacapillar
ThingDef.description: Timid by nature, this larva-like bug has a large thorax filled with putrescent gasses, allowing it to move about and escape attackers while barely touching the ground. It releases these gasses when attacked, often allowing it to escape unharmed. The gasses it contains also permit it to carry large loads, and many colonies in polluted areas use them as ridable pack animals.

ThingDef.label: crested dragon
ThingDef.description: Much like the prehistoric Parasaur, this lizard has a crest. The purpose is largely for display, but also allows them to make cute squeaky noises.

ThingDef.label: mahllik
ThingDef.description: A small, silkily furred, solitary grazer of the ice sheet, trailing long tassels of silky fur, a soft lump at rest that becomes a sudden, springing leap the instant danger closes.
